newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo slams attempts to "muzzle" him.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo slams attempts to "muzzle" him.

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, fresh from being fingerprinted by police in connection with one of many lawsuits against him, railed Wednesday against those seeking to "muzzle" his anti-corruption campaign.
Cavallo, who for five years steered economic reforms that tamed hyperinflation, accused the Justice Ministry of impeding investigations of graft.

"I regret to say that in many cases the Justice Ministry worked for there to be injustice," he told a packed audience of business leaders and economists at a luncheon sponsored by the Fundacion Mediterranea think-tank.
"Don't put a muzzle on people like me or prevent us from talking" about corruption cases, he added.

Since President Carlos Menem sacked his confrontational economy chief in July, Cavallo has announced he will run for Congress next year and launched an offensive against what he describes as widespread corruption.
He has accused Justice Minister Elias Jassan, Interior Minister Carlos Corach and presidential Chief of Staff Alberto Kohan of covering up official graft or manipulating judges.
The three have denied the charges and Corach has sued him.
Cavallo has also upset the administration with barbs against his successor, Roque Fernandez, suggesting he is weak and surrounded by a poor team of advisers.
Fernandez's top aide Carlos Rodriguez told reporters Wednesday not to confuse his boss's low-profile style with weakness or Cavallo's confrontational style with decisiveness.
But Cavallo insisted: "He needs people like I had....who had the courage and knowledge to put a brake on the things that did the country no good."
Earlier, Cavallo appeared at a Buenos Aires police station to have his fingerprints taken in a slander case and provide names of his neighbors who could testify about his lifestyle.
"I think they will ask my neighbors if I am a drunkard, if I take drugs, if I go out at night or if I live with my family," he told reporters outside.

Federal Judge Jorge Urso ordered Cavallo to appear on charges of slander filed by businessman Alfredo Yabran, whom Cavallo has accused of leading a "mafia" trying to take over the postal and customs services.
